pairing.title: Pair with your IDE

help.title: Pairing
help.text:
The QR code in the IDE's Remote Control window opens this page with a one-time code. The code never leaves the phone: it is removed from the address at once.

Compare the keys before you pair. The IDE key here must match the key in the Remote Control window. When the IDE asks you to approve this phone, it shows the phone key - it must match the one here.

After you approve, the phone and the IDE talk end-to-end encrypted through the relay, which only passes frames and cannot read them. Several IDEs can be paired with one phone.

An app added to the Home Screen keeps its own pairings, apart from Safari. To pair it, press and hold the link of the QR code in the camera, choose Copy Link and paste it on this screen.

machines.title: My IDEs

help.title: Remote Control
help.text:
Each IDE paired with this phone is listed here with its open and recent projects. Project folders never leave the computer: the phone knows a project by a key.

To add an IDE, open Remote Control in Agentic Workstation and scan its QR code with the phone camera.

Forget removes the pairing keys from this phone and tells the IDE to release it, if the IDE is reachable now. Otherwise revoke the phone in the IDE's Remote Control window.

notifications.title: Notifications

help.title: Notifications
help.text:
When this phone is not looking, a paired IDE can wake it: a conversation asks for a permission, a question or a plan, stops with an error or hits a usage limit, a scenario asks a question or a queue stops. Tapping the notification opens that conversation, queue or run. A finished turn does not notify.

The text is encrypted on the computer for this phone only. The relay and the push service of your phone see that a notification was sent, not what it says.

Turn off stops notifications from every IDE paired with this phone.

project.title: Project

help.title: Project
help.text:
Conversations are grouped by provider. Each shows what it is doing now and since when: working, needs you (a permission, a question or a plan) or idle. Past conversations can be opened and continued.

Scenario queues run scenarios one after another, in their own worktree or in the project folder. A recent project that is not open in the IDE shows only its queues.

help.title: Conversation
help.text:
The feed shows the end of the conversation as the IDE sees it, and updates live. Load earlier brings older messages from the IDE, a page at a time.

While Claude works, a new message waits in the IDE's queue and goes after the current turn. Stop next to the message field ends the turn.

A permission can be allowed once or denied. Allowing a tool always, bypass and auto modes, the terminal and ! commands are only available at the computer.

Tap a photo to see it large. A big photo comes reduced to fit the phone; the original stays in the IDE.

queue.title: Queue

help.title: Scenario queue
help.text:
A queue runs its scenarios one after another, in its own worktree or in the project folder.

Stop after current lets the running scenario finish, then the queue waits. A waiting item can stop the queue after itself, run only if the one before it succeeded, move up or down, or be removed.

Closing a queue and removing its worktree are only available at the computer.

run.title: Run

help.title: Scenario run
help.text:
A run is one pass of a scenario. Cards do the work, and the main thread (the head) reads what each card did and decides what comes next.

When the head asks you, answer here. Write to the head at the bottom: it reads your words between cards.

Pause keeps everything alive. Stop cuts the current card short. A stopped or failed run, or one waiting for a usage limit, can be continued.

start.title: Start a scenario

help.title: Start a scenario
help.text:
Pick a scenario from the project shelf or your personal shelf and answer its questions.

A new queue in its own worktree works on a separate branch, and the project files stay as they are. Without a worktree it works in the project folder. An existing queue runs the scenario after what is already in it.
